title: IntentTwin: Deconfounding Candidate Support and the Oracle-to-Deployment Gap in Offline Web Behavior Prediction
abstract: arXiv:2611.12918v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Offline web-behavior benchmarks frequently insert the demonstrated action into a finite candidate set and then measure reranking. We show that this protocol can create a candidate-support confound: when the target is outside training support while all distractors are sampled from that support, support membership identifies the gold action without modeling behavior. We formalize this effect with support-identifiability rate (SIR), construct support-balanced candidate sets, and evaluate a target-free dual-path proposer that combines support retrieval with open-vocabulary DOM/LM proposals. On filtered OPeRA (4,282/469/992 train/dev/test steps), the original protocol has SIR 1.0000 on target-OOV rows and a support-only rule reaches 1.0000 OOV Exact@1. Support balancing reduces SIR to 0.0000; the strongest conditional reranker obtains 0.7214 overall Exact@1, 0.7988 on IV rows, and 0.5668 on OOV rows. The target-free dual-path system reaches P

translated_title: IntentTwin：离线网页行为预测中候选支持去混杂与“理想评测到实际部署”的差距
translated_abstract: 离线网页行为基准测试通常将示范动作插入一个有限候选集，然后测量模型的重排序性能。我们证明这种协议会造成“候选支持混杂”问题：当目标动作位于训练支持集之外、而所有干扰项均从该支持集中采样时，仅凭支持集归属信息就能识别出正确动作，完全无需建模用户行为。我们用“支持可识别率”（SIR）将这一效应形式化，构建了支持均衡的候选集，并评估了一种免目标的双路径候选提议器，该提议器将支持集检索与开放词表的DOM/语言模型提议相结合。在过滤后的OPeRA数据集（训练/验证/测试分别为4,282/469/992步）上，原始协议在目标为词表外（OOV）的样本上SIR达到1.0000，仅用支持集规则即可取得1.0000的OOV Exact@1。支持均衡化将SIR降至0.0000；此时最强的条件重排序器总体Exact@1为0.7214，在词表内（IV）样本上为0.7988，在OOV样本上为0.5668。免目标双路径系统达到P（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文揭示了离线网页行为预测基准中仅凭候选动作是否属于训练支持集即可“作弊”答对的混杂效应，提出支持可识别率（SIR）这一度量、支持均衡候选集构建方法以及免目标双路径提议器，从而真实刻画从理想评测条件到实际部署的性能差距。
en_tdlr: This paper exposes a candidate-support confound in offline web-behavior benchmarks—where support membership alone identifies the gold action—introducing the support-identifiability rate (SIR), support-balanced candidate sets, and a target-free dual-path proposer to measure the true oracle-to-deployment gap.
